title: One Wall, 108 Windows — No Two Alike | Suzhou Gardens | China Travel Expert
description:
One garden wall in Suzhou holds 108 openwork windows — and no two share the same pattern.

The Canglang Pavilion (Surging Waves Pavilion) in Suzhou is famous for its 108 non-identical 漏窗 (lòuchuāng, "leaking windows"). Each lattice frames the garden beyond like a living painting; take one step and the composition changes — the classical design principle of 移步换景 ("every step, a new scene"). Suzhou's classical gardens were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997, celebrated as the finest expression of Chinese garden art, where architecture, rock, water and plants are composed like a scroll.

🧭 Expert Tip: Don't rush the corridors — stand still, then step slowly. Every window reframes the garden into a brand-new photo.

一堵墙，108扇漏窗，扇扇不同。
